# A deferred focus-leave from a menu's dismissal unmounts the same menu when it reopens within 50 ms

> **Current state, 2026-09-15.** Fixed by PR #18720, with the design below. This body is the record; the thread below it is history.

## The defect

A floating `menu.List` that is hidden and then shown again remounts, then gets taken down about 40 ms later with no user action. It's the same instance throughout (`setConfigs({hidden: true})`, then `({hidden: false})`), and it ends at `menuFocus: false, mounted: false, hidden: true`.

Repro: `test/playwright/component/menu/SpawnAnimation.spec.mjs` › *a dismissed and reopened instance is cleaned up and re-arms* failed 5–7 times in 60 serial repeats when this was filed, and once in CI, in the `components` job on PR #18325. On `dev@03219a75b7` it passed 60 of 60. That arm reopens only after polling for the removed node, and Playwright's first poll interval is 100 ms, which likely puts the reopen past the 50 ms gap. Reopening 0, 15, 30 or 45 ms after the node is gone failed 59 of 60 on the same tree.

## The mechanism, measured

1. The dismissal removes the focused menu from the DOM. The browser fires a native `focusout`, which reaches the app worker as a message.
2. `manager.Focus#onFocusout` defers delivery by `maxFocusInOutGap` (50 ms) and captures the component path as **ids** (`src/manager/Focus.mjs`).
3. The reopen remounts the same instance, with the same id, 8–16 ms after `hidden: false`. It requests focus asynchronously (`component.Base#afterSetMounted` → `focus()`). Its `focusin` has not reached the manager when the timer fires: `lastFocusInDate` was measured 10–18 ms older than `lastFocusOutDate`.
4. The timer fires 51–54 ms after the dismissal. The #18299 guard passes, because no newer focusout exists, and the ids resolve to the remounted instance.
5. `menu.List#onFocusLeave` takes the `!data.relatedTarget` branch and sets `menuFocus = false`, which makes `afterSetMenuFocus` unmount the menu.

A `MutationObserver` shows `REMOVED > ADDED > REMOVED` on every failure.

The reopened menu still holds `menuFocus: true`: hiding a component whose parent is not `document.body` removes its DOM through the parent's update (`component.Base#hide`), which never runs `menu.List#unmount()`. It also keeps `mounted: true`, because `VdomLifecycle#unmountRemovedChildren` skips floating children.

## Ruled out

| candidate | why |
|---|---|
| a newer focusout validating an older timer | real, and fixed by #18299 (PR #18301), but the failure rate did not move (7/60 → 6/60) |
| a mount generation on the instance, captured in `onFocusout` | built and unit-green, still 7/60 with and without it: the focusout reaches the worker after the remount, and the generation lives on the shared instance, so it has nothing to discriminate |
| `onFocusLeave` ignoring a leave whose path misses the current tree | same instance, same ids, so a stale path intersects the current tree anyway; `isInteractionPath` already implements that test |
| relaxing the `!data.relatedTarget` branch | it is the documented document-blur dismissal (`unit/menu/List.spec.mjs` › *keeps document blur and Escape as immediate dismissal paths*) |
| the `isConnected` the focusout already carries | Chromium fires `focusout` synchronously inside `node.remove()`, while the node is still connected and its path still reaches `window`, so a removal and a move send the same value (Playwright Chromium 153) |
| guarding on `mounted` | a floating component hidden through its parent's update keeps `mounted: true`, so a hidden menu and a shown one read the same |

## The fix

The worker only sees the order in which events **arrive**. The order in which they **happened** exists only on the main thread, at dispatch, so the stamp is added there.

- `DeltaUpdates#removeNode` records the id it is removing for the duration of `remove()`, and `DomEvents#onFocusOut` stamps a focusout raised inside that call with `removedNodeId`. No other focusout changes, so other focus consumers see the field only on a removal.
- `manager.Focus#isRemovedFloatingShownAgain`: a pending leave is not delivered when its removed node is a floating component that is shown again by the time the leave comes due. A floating component requests focus whenever it mounts (`component.Base#afterSetMounted`), so its new mount reports its own focus.
- Every other leave is delivered as before: a focusout without the stamp, a removed component that is still hidden, and a component that is not floating.

## Contract Ledger

`focusout.data.removedNodeId: String` is a new consumed field on the focusout payload the main thread sends to the app worker. It is additive and optional: it appears only on a focusout the engine's own node removal raised. Verified against PR #18720 at `f30ba0ee4b`.

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Behavior | Fallback / Edge Case | Docs | Evidence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Neo.main.DomEvents#onFocusOut` (producer) | this ticket | Stamps `data.removedNodeId` with `Neo.main.DeltaUpdates#removingNodeId`, the id that instance holds for the duration of its `node.remove()` call | Omitted entirely when no removal is in progress, so every other focusout keeps the shape it had | JSDoc on both members | `unit/main/DomEvents.spec.mjs` › *a focusout fired inside removeNode names the removed node, and one fired elsewhere does not* |
| `Neo.manager.Focus#isRemovedFloatingShownAgain` (consumer) | this ticket | A pending leave is dropped when `data.removedNodeId` resolves to a component that is `floating` and no longer `hidden` — its new mount reports its own focus | Falsy or unresolvable id, a removed component still hidden, and a non-floating one all return `false`, so the leave is delivered as before | JSDoc | `unit/manager/Focus.spec.mjs` › *the leave of a removed floating menu does not dismiss the menu once it is shown again*, and › *a removed menu that stays hidden, focus leaving a shown menu, and a non-floating remount all still dismiss* |

`manager.DomEvent` forwards the payload object as-is (it clones per listener with `Neo.clone(data, true, true)`), so the field needs no transport change. Nothing outside `manager.Focus` reads it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `SpawnAnimation.spec.mjs` › *a dismissed and reopened instance is cleaned up and re-arms* passes 60 serial repeats with zero failures.
- [ ] Red-first against the mechanism: an arm that delivers a leave raised against the previous mount to the remounted menu fails before the fix and passes after, without waiting on the race.
- [ ] Legitimate dismissals still dismiss: outside pointer (#17825), Escape, document blur and the leaf-click cascade, each named with the arm that covers it.
- [ ] No instrumentation is committed. Heavy probes perturb this race: per-transition stack capture took the repro from 7/60 to 0/30.

## Notes

- Instrument on the worker side. A main-realm `focusin`/`focusout` listener stays silent here, because the lifecycle runs in the app worker.
- Keep probes cheap. `getConfigs` on failure costs nothing. A `MutationObserver` on the body lowered the rate to 2/60, so read its shape, not its rate.
- Adjacent, not this defect: the `manager.Focus` dispatch reuses one `data` object across every component in the path, so a handler that retains it sees it change.

## Related

#18215 (the arm that surfaced it) · #18299 / PR #18301 (the superseded-focusout fix) · #17825 (outside-pointer dismissal) · PR #18720 (the fix)

## The `oldPath` contents kill fix-shape B

Captured on failure (3 in 60, `origin/dev@5a7cb7d1f1`):

```
leave own=neo-menu-list-1 related=false mounted=true
path=[neo-menu-list-1__neo-record-1, neo-menu-list-1, component-test-viewport, , , , ]
```

Three things it settles:

**1. The path contains the menu's OWN id.** `neo-menu-list-1` is in `oldPath`, so `leftPathIsOwnTree` is **also** true — the leave would have dismissed via the second disjunct even if the first did not exist. Weakening `!data.relatedTarget` alone changes nothing here.

**2. Fix-shape B is dead.** *"Ignore a leave whose `oldPath` does not intersect the current mounted tree"* cannot work: the id is **stable across the dismiss/reopen cycle**, so a stale leave from the previous lifecycle intersects the new tree perfectly. There is no positional information in the path that distinguishes the old mount from the new one. That leaves the generation-carrying shape as the only candidate on the table, and it now needs its own falsifier before anyone builds it.

**3. `mounted` is `true` when the leave lands.** The new instance is fully mounted, so this is not a leave racing an incomplete mount — it is a leave that is simply *about a different mount* and has no way to say so.

One loose end I am recording rather than explaining: the path has three real entries followed by **four empty strings** (`oldPathLen=7`, of which 4 are `''`). I do not know whether those are placeholders, stale slots, or an artefact of how the path is assembled during an unmount. If they carry lifecycle information, they may be the very thing a generation guard could key on — but that is a guess, and the next person should measure it rather than inherit it from me.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-04T14:59:42Z

## The mechanism is in `manager/Focus.mjs`, not the menu — a deferred leave re-resolves stale ids to live instances

This is not a `menu.List` defect. The menu is where it is *visible*.

### The line

`src/manager/Focus.mjs`, `onFocusout`:

```js
onFocusout(opts) {
    me.lastFocusOutDate = new Date();

    me.timeout(me.maxFocusInOutGap).then(() => {
        if (me.lastFocusOutDate > me.lastFocusInDate) {
            me.focusLeave(opts)          // ← `opts` captured 50ms ago
        }
    })
}
```

`maxFocusInOutGap` is **50** (`:39`). The leave is deferred half a frame-and-a-bit to distinguish a real departure from a focus *move* — reasonable, and the debounce is not the problem.

The problem is what `opts` carries and how it is redeemed. `opts.componentPath` is an array of **ids**, and 50 ms later `setComponentFocus` does:

```js
components = opts.componentPath.map(id => Neo.getComponent(id))
```

**Ids are stable across unmount and remount.** So a leave raised against the *old* mount resolves, at dispatch time, to whichever instance holds that id *now* — the new one.

### The chain, end to end

1. `hidden: true` → menu unmounts → DOM `focusout` → leave scheduled for +50 ms, path captured as ids.
2. `hidden: false` → menu remounts **with the same id**, takes focus, `menuFocus` → true.
3. The timer fires. `focusLeave(opts)` runs with the stale path.
4. `Neo.getComponent(id)` hands back the **new** instance.
5. `onFocusLeave` lands on it with `relatedTarget: null` → `menuFocus = false` → `unmount()`.

**The timings agree.** Measured removal is 35–46 ms after mount; the deferral window is 50 ms. The removal sits inside it every time.

It also explains the Heisenbug exactly: adding `new Error().stack` per transition pushed the remount later relative to a fixed 50 ms timer, so the leave fired before the remount existed and hit nothing. 0/30 was not the bug going away — it was the race being won.

### What is measured, read, and still inferred

- **Measured:** the instance trail (7/7 identical), removal at 35–46 ms, `oldPath` contents, `mounted=true` at leave, `maxFocusInOutGap` = 50.
- **Read from source:** the deferral, and that ids are re-resolved to components at dispatch time rather than instances being captured at raise time.
- **Still inferred, and I have NOT logged it:** that `lastFocusOutDate > lastFocusInDate` is true when the timer fires in our case. It must be for the branch to be taken, but I have not instrumented those two dates. Anyone building the fix should confirm it before assuming the date comparison is the discriminator — it may be that the remount's focusin never reaches the manager at all, which is a different repair.

### What this changes about scope

The blast radius is not menus. **Any** component that unmounts and remounts under a stable id inside 50 ms can receive a leave raised against its predecessor. Menus surface it because `menu.List` turns a leave into an `unmount()`; a component that merely toggles a CSS class on leave would show nothing and still be wrong.

The fix belongs at the raise/redeem seam in `manager/Focus.mjs` — capture what identifies the mount, and drop the dispatch when the id now resolves to a different one — not in `menu.List`, whose handling of a leave it legitimately receives is correct.

Retitling and re-scoping this ticket accordingly.

## The date branch is confirmed — and it corrects two things I wrote

I flagged one link as inferred: *"that `lastFocusOutDate > lastFocusInDate` is true when the timer fires… I have not instrumented those two dates."* Instrumented now. 6 failures in 60, and the two captured records agree:

```
timer out=1788534020938  lastOut=1788534020938  lastIn=1788534020928  outNewer=true  path=[neo-menu-list-1,component-test-viewport]
timer out=1788534038308  lastOut=1788534038308  lastIn=1788534038290  outNewer=true  path=[neo-menu-list-1,component-test-viewport]
```

Three readings, and two of them correct me.

**1. The branch is taken, and it is the original leave.** `outNewer=true`, and the captured `outAt` equals `lastFocusOutDate` at fire time — no newer focusout intervened. Confirmed as inferred.

**2. The reopened menu never takes focus. I said it did, and that was wrong.** `lastIn` is **10 ms and 18 ms EARLIER** than `lastOut` — the manager's last focusin predates the focusout that scheduled the leave. Nothing focuses the menu after the reopen.

Which means my reading of the instance trail was wrong too. It shows a single `setMenuFocus false->true`, and I attributed it to the remount. It belongs to the **first** open. The corrected sequence:

1. Menu opens, takes focus, `menuFocus` → true.
2. `hidden: true` → unmount → `focusout` → leave scheduled for +50 ms, `componentPath` captured as ids.
3. `hidden: false` → menu remounts **and is never focused**. No focusin reaches the manager.
4. Timer fires; `lastOut > lastIn` still holds — and it holds *because* step 3 raised no focusin, not because of a race between two focus events.
5. `Neo.getComponent('neo-menu-list-1')` resolves the stale id to the **new** instance; `onFocusLeave` lands on it; `menuFocus` true → false; `unmount()`.

So this is not two focus events racing. It is **one** leave, correctly scheduled against a mount that no longer exists, redeemed against an id that now means something else. Cleaner than my earlier account and worse in implication: no focus activity on the new mount is required for it to be taken down.

**3. I conflated two different paths.** `componentPath` here is **2 entries** — `[neo-menu-list-1, component-test-viewport]` — not the 7-entry `oldPath` I reported earlier. `oldPath` is the DOM event path (`opts.data.path`, which is why it carries empty strings); `componentPath` is the component-id chain, and **`componentPath` is the one that gets re-resolved**. My "the path contains the menu's own id" observation happens to hold for both, so the conclusion survived, but I was reading the wrong array when I made it.

### What this settles for the fix

The discriminator cannot be the date comparison — it is behaving correctly given the events it saw. The defect is that `componentPath` is a list of **ids redeemed late**. Capturing what identifies the *mount* at raise time, and dropping the dispatch when an id now resolves to a different one, addresses it without touching the 50 ms debounce or any `menu.List` predicate.

That is the only shape still standing, and it now has no unmeasured link in front of it.

## Why the remount's focus loses, and the precedent the fix should follow

Two last pieces. The mechanism now has no unmeasured link and no invented shape.

### The remount *does* try to take focus — asynchronously, against a fixed timer

`component/Base.mjs#afterSetMounted`, on the mount branch:

```js
if (me.floating) {
    me.alignTo();
    // Focus will be pushed into the first input field or other focusable item
    me.focus(me.id, true)
}
```

and on the unmount branch, `me.revertFocus()` — which is what raises the `focusout` that schedules the leave.

So the reopen is not passive. It calls `focus()`. But `focus()` is a worker→main→DOM round-trip, while `maxFocusInOutGap` is a flat **50 ms** measured from the focusout. When the round-trip's resulting `focusin` does not get back to the manager inside the remaining window, `lastFocusOutDate > lastFocusInDate` still holds and the stale leave fires. My measurement caught exactly that state: `lastIn` 10–18 ms *older* than `lastOut` at fire time.

That closes the last question. It is an **async focus acquisition racing a fixed synchronous deadline**, which is why it is load-dependent, why it sits at ~40 ms, and why adding per-transition instrumentation made it vanish.

It also means the earlier framing *"the remount is never focused"* is imprecise in a way worth fixing: it **requests** focus and loses. Same outcome, different repair surface — you cannot fix this by making the menu take focus, because it already asks.

### The fix has a precedent in this exact file — do not invent one

`component/Base.mjs:337` already carries the shape this needs:

```js
/**
 * Monotonic guard for registerNativeDragZone's mount-gated sends: a pending send
 * whose generation no longer matches was superseded (reset, replaced, or moved) and drops.
 */
nativeDragZoneGeneration = 0
```

used at `:674` (`gen = ++me.nativeDragZoneGeneration`), `:676` (`if (gen === me.nativeDragZoneGeneration && …)`) and `:695`. A pending async operation captures the generation at raise time and drops itself at redeem time if it no longer matches.

That is precisely the defect here — a pending async dispatch redeemed after the state it was raised against is gone — and the codebase has already solved it once, in the same class, for the same reason. **Whoever implements this should follow that pattern rather than designing a new one**, and should check whether the guard belongs on the component (a mount generation bumped in `afterSetMounted`) or on the manager's captured `opts`. Instance identity will **not** work: the menu is the same object across `hidden` true→false, so only a mount-scoped counter discriminates.

### Ticket state

The mechanism is fully measured. The fix shape has a named in-repo precedent. AC-2's red-first arm is now writable without waiting on the race: bump a mount generation, dispatch a leave captured against the previous one, and assert it does not reach the component.

I am leaving the implementation unclaimed-in-detail rather than half-building it at the end of a long session — the ticket now contains everything needed to start, which is what I would want to inherit.

## I built the generation guard. It does not fix this. Reporting the negative.

The fix shape I argued for two comments ago is implemented, its unit arm is green, and **the component flake is unchanged**. Nothing is being shipped.

### The numbers

| tree | failures / 60 serial repeats |
|---|---|
| `origin/dev` | **7** |
| with the mount-generation guard | **7** |

Identical. One earlier run gave 5/60, but it overlapped a concurrent unit suite, so I discarded it and re-measured with nothing else running. 7 either way.

### What was built, and it does work

- `component.Base#mountGeneration`, monotonic, bumped on the mount branch of `afterSetMounted` — following the `nativeDragZoneGeneration` precedent at `:337` rather than inventing a shape.
- `manager.Focus#onFocusout` captures each path entry's generation at raise, and at redeem drops only the entries whose generation moved, preserving the rest.

A red-first unit pair covers it: a leave deferred across a remount is dropped (fails without the guard, passes with it), and — the control that makes the first arm mean something — **an ordinary deferred leave is still delivered**, so a guard that dropped everything would fail. 47/47 green across the focus and menu unit surface.

### The guard's input is correct, which is what makes this interesting

Measured on the live fixture, no failure required:

```
after open    mountGeneration=1  mounted=true   hidden=false
after hide    mountGeneration=1  mounted=false  hidden=true
after reopen  mountGeneration=2  mounted=true   hidden=false
```

The generation bumps exactly as designed. The guard is *able* to discriminate the old mount from the new one, and the flake persists anyway.

### What that localizes

If the guard can tell the mounts apart and still drops nothing, then at the moment `onFocusout` runs, the generation it records is **already the new one**. The focusout handler is executing *after* the remount, not before it.

Which means my premise was wrong in a specific way worth stating: I assumed the leave is *raised* against the old mount and *redeemed* against the new one, so capturing at raise would fix it. The measurement says the raise is already too late. `revertFocus()` runs during unmount, but the DOM focusout it provokes reaches the manager after the reopen has landed — so there is no point inside `manager.Focus` at which the old mount is still current.

A guard at the raise/redeem seam therefore cannot work, however it is keyed. The discriminator has to come from something that knows *when focus actually left*, which the focusout handler does not.

### Disposition

Branch not pushed, no PR. A primitive with no working consumer is accretion, and a PR would claim a fix that 7/60 says does not exist.

What survives for the next attempt: the mechanism trail is still valid (leave → `menuFocus false` → `unmount`), the generation approach is now **eliminated with evidence** rather than untried, and the question is narrowed to one thing — why the focusout handler runs after the remount, and whether anything upstream of it retains the pre-unmount ordering.

The AC-2 arm I wrote is reusable by whoever takes that on; it is in the ticket's history, not in `dev`.

I would rather report a measured non-fix than ship a plausible one. The 7/60 is what a red-first unit arm cannot tell you.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-04T15:37:31Z

## Why the raise is late, and why this is bigger than a guard

Closing out my narrowing so the next person starts where I stopped rather than where I started.

### The focusout is the browser's, not ours

`component.Base#revertFocus` only acts under a condition:

```js
revertFocus() {
    let relatedTarget = this.focusEnterData?.relatedTarget;

    if (this.containsFocus && relatedTarget) {
        Neo.getComponent(relatedTarget.id)?.focus()
    }
}
```

Read from source, **not measured**: for a menu opened programmatically there may be no `focusEnterData.relatedTarget` at all, in which case this is a no-op and does not originate the focusout. I did not instrument which branch is taken, and the next person should before relying on it.

Either way the focusout that matters is the **native** one: removing a focused node from the DOM makes the browser move focus to `body` and fire the event. That happens on the main thread, when the vdom update is applied — and then travels to the worker as a message.

### Which is why no guard at the manager can fix this

The reopen (`hidden: false`) is its own worker→main round-trip. So two independent crossings race:

- the native focusout, main → worker, triggered by the removal;
- the remount, worker → main → worker.

`manager.Focus` sees them in arrival order and has no way to recover the order they *occurred* in. That is consistent with everything measured: the guard's input is correct (`mountGeneration` 1 → 1 → 2), and it still drops nothing, because by the time `onFocusout` runs the remount has already landed.

**A DOM event cannot carry mount identity, because the DOM does not have one.** The information needed to discriminate is lost at the boundary, before any worker-side code — guard, generation, or otherwise — gets to look at it.

### What a real fix would have to do

Stamp the event where the ordering still exists: on the **main thread**, at dispatch, with something identifying the node/vnode generation the focus actually left. The worker could then discard a leave whose stamp refers to DOM that is already gone.

That is a change to the main-thread event pipeline, affecting every focus consumer — not a menu fix and not a manager fix. Per the escalation ladder that is high-blast and cross-substrate, so it wants a Discussion and a design before an implementation, rather than a solo PR from me at the end of a long session.

### Ticket state

- **Mechanism:** measured end to end, unchanged.
- **Generation guard:** built, unit-green, **eliminated by measurement** — 7/60 both with and without.
- **Root of the elimination:** the discriminating information is lost at the worker boundary.
- **Direction:** stamp at main-thread dispatch; needs design, not a patch.

I am leaving this open and unclaimed for implementation. The AC-2 arm and the generation primitive are recoverable from this ticket's history if the design lands that way, and should not be resurrected before it does — a primitive with no working consumer is accretion.

## Negative result — I found a real stale-leave defect, fixed it, and the symptom did not move

**AC-1: 6 failures in 60. The pre-fix rate was 7 in 60.** That is not a fix; it is noise.

Retracting the causal claim I broadcast at 17:42Z. I said the menu symptom "is a `manager/Focus` delivery bug, not a menu predicate bug — RED-FIRST ARM PROVES IT." The arm proves the delivery bug **exists**. It never proved that bug **causes this ticket's symptom**, and the 60-repeat measurement now falsifies that step. Two tiers of red-first green do not make a candidate a cure.

### What was actually found, and it is real

`src/manager/Focus.mjs#onFocusout` defers delivery by `maxFocusInOutGap` (50), and the pending timer closes over its own `opts` while gating on **manager-global** dates:

```js
me.lastFocusOutDate = new Date();
me.timeout(me.maxFocusInOutGap).then(() => {
    if (me.lastFocusOutDate > me.lastFocusInDate) { me.focusLeave(opts) }
})
```

A *newer* focusout moves `lastFocusOutDate` past `lastFocusInDate` and thereby satisfies an *older* timer's check on its behalf — delivering stale `opts`. Red-first arm, added to `test/playwright/unit/manager/Focus.spec.mjs`, which had no coverage of deferred delivery at all:

```
Expected value: not "focus-stale-child"
Received array: ["focus-stale-child", "focus-stale-root", "focus-stale-other"]
```

The stale focusout delivered to its entire componentPath. Requiring timer identity (`me.lastFocusOutDate === date`) turns it green, and the full unit suite is **3185/3185** with the change.

`getConfigs` is already a remote on `worker.App`, so reading the triple on failure adds **zero** per-transition worker cost. ## Mount trail measured: it mounts, then something takes it down at the 50 ms boundary

The fork I left open — *mounted-then-unmounted* vs *the reopen never landed* — is resolved. Main-realm `MutationObserver` on the subject id, run against `dev@097d90f383` (i.e. with #18299's guard merged):

| run | dismissal `REMOVED` | reopen `ADDED` | second `REMOVED` | Δ from dismissal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 240 | 248 (+8) | 294 | **54 ms** |
| 2 | 335 | 351 (+16) | 386 | **51 ms** |

Shape `REMOVED > ADDED > REMOVED` on **2 of 2** failures, terminal state `menuFocus=false, mounted=false, hidden=true` both times.

**So the reopen lands.** The menu mounts 8–16 ms after `hidden: false`, and is then taken back down. The "never mounted" branch is eliminated, and the ADDED→REMOVED deltas (46 ms, 35 ms) sit inside this ticket's originally recorded band of *"ADDED 5–10 ms after the reopen, REMOVED 35–46 ms later"* — unchanged by #18299.

### The number that matters

Measured from the **dismissal**, not from the mount: **54 ms and 51 ms.**

`maxFocusInOutGap` is **50**. The takedown lands on the far side of that boundary, both times.

That is the single-focusout survivor I described in my previous comment, now with timing rather than reasoning behind it. The dismissal raises a focusout at t≈0 and arms a timer for t≈50. The reopen mounts at t≈8–16 and takes focus. At t≈50 the timer fires — and #18299's guard cannot stop it, because:

```js
if (me.lastFocusOutDate === date && date > me.lastFocusInDate) { me.focusLeave(opts) }
```

there is **no superseding focusout**, so `lastFocusOutDate === date` holds trivially; and the reopen's focusin evidently has not yet moved `lastFocusInDate` past it. The timer is the newest one. It is simply stale with respect to a **mount** it has no way to see — which is exactly the reframing I proposed: the missing key is *which mount*, not *which focusout*.

`hidden: true` in the terminal state is therefore `unmount()`'s write, not a `hidden: false` that never landed.

### One honesty note on the rate

Failure rates across the four 60-repeat runs: **7/60** (pre-fix baseline) → **6/60** (post-fix) → **5/60** (post-fix + `getConfigs` probe) → **2/60** (post-fix + `MutationObserver` probe).

2/60 is the lowest of the four and I am **not** claiming it as evidence of improvement. A `MutationObserver` on `document.body` subtree does main-thread work, and this is a timing-gated defect — mild perturbation is the likelier reading, in the same direction as the stack-capture attempt that took the repro to 0/30, just far weaker. **Treat the shape from this run as the finding and the rate as unreliable.** The shape is what 2/2 agreement supports; the rate is not.

### Where that leaves the fix

The manager holds no mount identity, so it cannot currently distinguish "this leave belongs to the mount that raised it" from "this leave belongs to a mount that has since been replaced." Two shapes worth weighing, each with its falsifier — I am not prescribing one here:

| Shape | Falsifier |
|---|---|
| A remount invalidates any pending leave targeting that component — the manager learns about mounts | If nothing notifies `manager.Focus` on mount, this needs a new signal, and that is a wider change than the defect warrants |
| `onFocusLeave` ignores a leave whose `oldPath` does not intersect the component's CURRENT mounted tree — the intersection is already computed at `menu/List.mjs:530` as `leftPathIsOwnTree`, but used as a dismissal TRIGGER rather than a guard | If a legitimate dismissal can present a non-intersecting `oldPath`, this suppresses real dismissals — check against the document-blur arm (`unit/menu/List.spec.mjs:173`) and #17825 before adopting |

Shape B is the cheaper one and the intersection test already exists in the consumer; whether inverting its role is safe is precisely what the two named arms decide, and that is the next measurement rather than an assumption.

Instrumentation reverted; the tracked tree carries nothing from it (AC-4). Ticket stays open and stays mine.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-05T12:43:20Z

## Shape 2 is eliminated — and the reason is the same one that killed the mount-generation guard

The Fix table left shape 2's falsifier unchecked: *"if a legitimate dismissal also presents a non-intersecting `oldPath`, this suppresses real dismissals."* I went to check that and found the shape fails one step earlier, for a structural reason, so the falsifier never gets its turn.

**The reopen is the same instance.** `SpawnAnimation.spec.mjs` captures the id once and toggles `hidden` on it:

```js
menuId = await createMenu(page, {animateSpawn: true});
await page.evaluate(id => Neo.worker.App.setConfigs({id, hidden: true}),  menuId);
await page.evaluate(id => Neo.worker.App.setConfigs({id, hidden: false}), menuId);
```

Dismiss and reopen are two mounts of **one** instance, and the trail agrees — `setMenuFocus undefined->false` appears once, as construction, not once per open.

**So there is no id-based discriminator, by construction.** Shape 2 asks `onFocusLeave` to ignore a leave whose `oldPath` does not intersect the currently mounted tree. The previous mount and the current mount are the same components with the same ids, so a stale `oldPath` intersects the current tree *exactly as strongly as a fresh one does*. The comparison returns the same answer in both states — which makes it not a discriminator at all, whatever its effect on legitimate dismissals.

That is also, I now think, **why the mount-generation guard measured 7/60 with and 7/60 without.** It was not a weak guard; it was a guard with nothing to read. The generation lives on the instance, and the instance is shared by both lifecycles — so at the moment the leave arrives, the menu cannot tell which of its own mounts raised it. The information is not degraded locally, it was never local.

### What this does to the ticket

Both locally-scoped candidate shapes are now eliminated, each for the same underlying reason:

| Shape | Status |
|---|---|
| mount-generation guard on the instance | eliminated by measurement (7/60 → 7/60) |
| `oldPath` ∩ current mounted tree | **eliminated structurally** — same instance, same ids, no discriminating answer |

The parked rationale in the body was right, and it is now right for a stated reason rather than by elimination of one attempt: **the fix has to live where the leave is matched to a mount, because that is the last place the ordering still exists.** Nothing inside `menu/List.mjs` can recover it.

### Boundary on this claim

The instance-identity fact is read from the arm's source, not from re-instrumenting the failing run — AC-4 records that per-transition stack capture takes the repro from 7/60 to 0/30, so I did not re-run a probe to confirm `oldPath`'s contents. The argument does not need them: a discriminator built on id intersection cannot work when both lifecycles carry identical ids, whatever the path happens to hold.

Still **unowned and still parked**, on the same rationale — the remaining shape is a change to the main-thread focus-event pipeline, which is high-blast, touches every focus consumer, and wants a Discussion before an implementation. This comment narrows what that Discussion has to decide; it does not open it.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-08T19:38:47Z

## Both falsifiers run at source: **shape B is eliminated, and it already exists**. The park was correct.

Not claiming the lane — the body's `unowned-rationale:` is sound and this does not change it. Running the two falsifiers the ticket attached to its candidate shapes, because that is measurement rather than implementation and it is what a Discussion would otherwise have to derive.

### The mechanism is no longer a reading — it is confirmed at source

The body states the stale-leave explanation as *"the strong reading, stated as a reading and not as measured"*. Three lines settle it:

| | |
|---|---|
| `src/manager/Focus.mjs:78-79` | `@param {Array} opts.componentPath` — **"Component ids upwards"**. The path is ids, not instances |
| `src/manager/Focus.mjs:100` | the leave path is derived from `history[0].componentPath` — a **previous** focus state |
| `src/manager/Focus.mjs:192` | `components = opts.componentPath.map(id => Neo.getComponent(id))` — resolved **at dispatch**, not at raise |

So a leave raised against one mount is delivered to whatever instance holds that id when it is finally dispatched. That is the ticket's title, and it is now source-backed rather than inferred.

### Falsifier A — *"the focus manager has no generation to carry"*

**Fires.** The dispatched payload is built at `:189-207` and carries `relatedTarget`, `component` and `oldPath`/`path`. There is **no generation, no timestamp, and no instance identity** other than what `Neo.getComponent(id)` yields at dispatch time. Shape A therefore cannot key on anything that exists today — it requires *adding* a stamp to the pipeline, which is precisely the high-blast change the body parked. **The park is confirmed, not overturned.**

*(Adjacent, observed and not diagnosed: `data` at `:189` is a single object mutated inside the `forEach` — `data.component` is reassigned per component and the same reference is handed to every handler and fired as the event payload. Any consumer retaining it sees it change underneath. Not this ticket's defect and I am not chasing it.)*

### Falsifier B — and it is stronger than the ticket expected

The proposed shape is *"`onFocusLeave` ignores a leave whose `oldPath` does not intersect the CURRENT mounted tree"*. **That predicate already exists and is already wired.** `src/menu/List.mjs:402`, `isInteractionPath(path)`:

```js
const ids = new Set(path.map(item => item.id).filter(Boolean));
let root = this;
while (root.parentMenu) { root = root.parentMenu }
const menus = [root];
while ((menu = menus.pop())) {
    if (ids.has(menu.id)) return true;
    Object.values(menu.subMenuMap || {}).forEach(submenu => submenu?.mounted && menus.push(submenu))
}
```

It is a by-id intersection test against the live menu tree, and `onFocusLeave` calls it as its **third disjunct** — unreachable in the failing trail only because `!data.relatedTarget` short-circuits first, exactly as the body says.

**And it would not help if it were reachable.** The leave path is the *previous focus path*, built as ids upwards from the previously-focused node — so it contains the menu's own id, and the reopened instance reuses that id. That reuse is the very reason late resolution delivers the leave to the new instance. An intersection test therefore returns **true** for the stale leave, and `!isInteractionPath(...)` is **false**: shape B is a no-op against this defect by construction.

*(Boundary: the last step is derived from how `componentPath` is built, not read off a captured payload — the trail records `oldPathLen=7` without its contents. If a repro ever prints that path, it is a one-line confirmation.)*

So shape B is eliminated for a better reason than the one the ticket anticipated. It was going to be weighed against *"does this suppress legitimate dismissals"* — the answer to that is also no (the documented document-blur arm passes `oldPath: [{id: root.id}]`, which intersects), but it never gets that far, because it cannot suppress the target case either.

### Where this leaves the design

**One surviving shape**, and it is the parked one: a leave must carry the mount it was raised against, which means stamping it in `manager/Focus` where the ordering still exists. Every focus consumer is downstream of that payload, so the body's judgement that this wants a Discussion before an implementation stands — now with one candidate removed rather than two open.

Nothing committed, and no instrumentation added: AC-4 rules that out, and the measurement above needed none.
